note: Source revision at build time. Hashes describe the generated content, including local edits. The documentation tracks the main branch and may describe features newer than the latest published release.

pages.title: What is ZeroJ?
pages.description: ZeroJ is a Java-first zero-knowledge proof toolkit for Cardano. Learn what it does, how the pieces fit, and where to start.

pages.title: Installation
pages.description: Add ZeroJ to a Gradle or Maven project with the BOM, wire up the annotation processor, and enable the dev-only trusted setup for local runs.

pages.title: Quickstart: your first proof
pages.description: In about ten minutes, prove you know a secret factor without revealing it, then verify the proof in pure Java. Circuit, witness, setup, prove, verify.

pages.title: Status & maturity
pages.description: What ZeroJ's Beta, Experimental, Disabled and Assurance-only labels mean, the full support matrix, and what "not for production" means in practice.

pages.title: Zero-knowledge in plain English
pages.description: What a zero-knowledge proof is, what it convinces you of, what it can't do, and a mental model that maps it onto ordinary Java code.

pages.title: Circuits, constraints & witnesses
pages.description: How ZK circuits really work (equations over a finite field, R1CS, witnesses), why Java control flow doesn't apply, and how under-constrained circuits break.

pages.title: Groth16, PlonK & BBS
pages.description: The three proof systems in ZeroJ, how their setup, proof size and verification cost differ, and why Cardano uses the BLS12-381 curve.

pages.title: Trusted setup, explained
pages.description: What a trusted setup is, why its "toxic waste" can forge proofs, how multi-party ceremonies remove the risk, and what ZeroJ provides for dev and production.

pages.title: ZK on Cardano
pages.description: How Cardano verifies ZK proofs with Plutus V3 BLS12-381 builtins, how proofs map onto eUTxO, what it costs, and why a valid proof is not authorization.

pages.title: Commitments & encryption, explained
pages.description: Sealed envelopes, lockboxes and shared keys: what Pedersen commitments, ElGamal encryption, confidential notes and threshold decryption do, in plain English.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: Short, plain-English definitions of the zero-knowledge, cryptography and Cardano terms used throughout the ZeroJ docs.

pages.title: Prove you're over 18
pages.description: Build a range proof with ZkUInt, see why bit widths matter, test an invalid witness, and verify with nothing but a key, a proof and public inputs.

pages.title: Private allowlist with a Merkle tree
pages.description: Prove you're on a list without saying who you are, using a Poseidon Merkle tree, then add a nullifier so each member can act only once per event.

pages.title: Verify your proof on Cardano
pages.description: Lock test ADA behind a Groth16 verifier on a local Yaci DevKit devnet, unlock it with a proof, and learn why a bare verifier must never guard real value.

pages.title: Bring circom & snarkjs circuits
pages.description: Prove a circom circuit with ZeroJ's pure-Java prover using snarkjs keys, and hand ZeroJ proofs to snarkjs. Groth16 on BLS12-381, both directions.

pages.title: Choose how to disclose
pages.description: Six ways to share private data on Cardano with ZeroJ, and what each party learns: reveal signed values, prove a rule, hide a number, tell chosen readers, encrypt for an auditor, or split the trust.

pages.title: Reveal the value (BBS)
pages.description: Show a verifier some attributes of an issuer-signed credential exactly as issued, and hide the rest, with BBS signatures. No circuit, no trusted setup.

pages.title: Prove a rule (Groth16 predicates)
pages.description: Prove a yes/no fact about private data, such as an age, income or score threshold, from a signed or committed credential, without revealing the data. The verifier learns only the answer.

pages.title: Hide a number (Pedersen commitments)
pages.description: Publish a number as a sealed commitment, prove facts about it, add commitments together and open them later, so balances, bids and totals stay private on a public ledger.

pages.title: Tell chosen readers (confidential notes)
pages.description: Put a hidden amount on-chain and seal its opening separately for each reader, such as the owner and an auditor, so they can read it straight from the chain and nobody else can.

pages.title: Encrypt for an auditor (ElGamal + proof)
pages.description: Encrypt a value to an auditor's key and prove the ciphertext matches the hidden amount, so the auditor can always read the real value and the sender can't under-report.

pages.title: Split the trust (threshold decryption)
pages.description: Encrypt values to a key that no single party holds, so only a quorum of trustees can decrypt, and agree to decrypt only the result, such as an election tally.

pages.title: Write circuits with annotations
pages.description: Author ZeroJ circuits as annotated Java classes, and use the generated companion to build, fill inputs, compute witnesses, and wire proofs.

pages.title: CircuitSpec & the Signal DSL
pages.description: Write circuits directly with CircuitSpec, Signal and the inline CircuitAPI DSL, compile them, compute witnesses, and use hints without breaking soundness.

pages.title: Gadget library
pages.description: The circuit building blocks in zeroj-circuit-lib (hashes, Merkle proofs, ranges, Jubjub, and Cardano key derivation), with status and cost.

pages.title: Test your circuits for soundness
pages.description: Why honest-witness tests aren't enough, a soundness checklist, invalid-witness and proof-tampering JUnit tests, and differential testing.

pages.title: Prove with Groth16
pages.description: Set up keys, generate Groth16 proofs on BLS12-381, scale to millions of constraints, and export proofs and keys for verifiers.

pages.title: Run a trusted setup ceremony
pages.description: Run a multi-party Groth16 ceremony with snarkjs and the zeroj-ceremony tool, import the result into ZeroJ, and know what to check before trusting one.

pages.title: Performance & large circuits
pages.description: How ZeroJ's pure-Java Groth16 prover handles millions of constraints, how to size memory, when the optional blst backend helps, and JVM and GraalVM notes.

pages.title: Prove with PlonK
pages.description: What ZeroJ's experimental PlonK support contains today, how to try it off-chain, and its known gaps. Groth16 is the supported path.

pages.title: Verify proofs in Java
pages.description: Verify Groth16 proofs off-chain with ZeroJ's proof model, verifier backends and registries, and build a service that only trusts keys you pinned.

pages.title: Verify proofs on Cardano
pages.description: Run Groth16 verification inside a Plutus V3 validator with zeroj-onchain-julc, bind proofs to the spend, and plan budgets and reference scripts.

pages.title: Secure your ZK application
pages.description: A practical threat-model checklist for ZeroJ builders — authorization, replay, nullifiers, trusted inputs, setup, circuit soundness and secrets.

pages.title: Selective disclosure with BBS
pages.description: Issue BBS credentials, derive presentations that reveal only chosen attributes, verify them in Java or on Cardano, and bind them against replay.

pages.title: Large authenticated state (Poseidon MPF/JMT)
pages.description: Keep millions of entries off-chain, publish one Poseidon root, and prove single-key reads and updates with small Groth16 circuits. Experimental.

pages.title: Pedersen commitments
pages.description: Commit to a hidden number, open it later, add commitments together, and prove facts about the hidden value in a Groth16 circuit, with ZeroJ's pedersen-jubjub-v1 profile.

pages.title: ElGamal encryption
pages.description: Encrypt small amounts to someone's public key, add ciphertexts without decrypting them, and prove in a Groth16 circuit what a ciphertext contains, with ZeroJ's elgamal-jubjub-v1 profile.

pages.title: Threshold decryption
pages.description: Split an ElGamal key among trustees so that no single party can decrypt, run the distributed key generation, deliver its private shares over a public board with HPKE, and decrypt only a total.

pages.title: Confidential notes
pages.description: Put a Pedersen commitment on-chain together with its opening, encrypted separately for the owner and each auditor, then recover notes by scanning the chain with a viewing key.

pages.title: Use cases
pages.description: What zero-knowledge proofs, commitments and encryption unlock on Cardano — thirteen worked use cases, the building block behind each, and runnable demos.

pages.title: Private voting
pages.description: Let each eligible member vote exactly once, keep every choice secret, and publish only the total, using Merkle membership, nullifiers, ElGamal-encrypted ballots and Groth16 on Cardano.

pages.title: Proof of reserves
pages.description: A custodian proves its reserves cover every customer balance without publishing any balance, and each customer can check they were counted.

pages.title: Age & KYC eligibility
pages.description: Prove you're old enough and live in an approved country, using an issuer-signed credential, while the validator learns only "eligible".

pages.title: Private NFT ownership
pages.description: Prove you hold an NFT from a collection for one-time token-gated access, without revealing which NFT or which wallet, and see why the nullifier must absorb a holder secret.

pages.title: One claim per person
pages.description: A Sybil-resistant airdrop where each personhood credential claims once per round with a nullifier even the issuer can't link to a person, and the payout bound to the proved recipient.

pages.title: Selective disclosure & reusable KYC
pages.description: Do KYC once, then show each service only what it asks for, as Groth16 predicates over hidden fields or BBS presentations verified on Cardano.

pages.title: Digital product passport
pages.description: An auditor commits to each product measurement with a Pedersen commitment; the manufacturer proves carbon, recycled-content, origin and inspection claims against them, and one co-signed Cardano transaction mints a locked passport record.

pages.title: Prove you own a Cardano account
pages.description: Prove you know the wallet root key behind a Cardano address, without revealing the seed or signing anything, so a refund can reach the real owner.

pages.title: Private token transfers
pages.description: A design walkthrough of a shielded pool on Cardano. Deposit, then withdraw to a fresh address that nobody can link to the deposit. Design only, no demo.

pages.title: Confidential payroll
pages.description: Pay salaries on Cardano without publishing them, while the tax authority reads every salary from the chain and the employer can't under-report one.

pages.title: Sealed-bid auction
pages.description: Bids stay hidden from other bidders and the public, every bid is readable by the auctioneer from the moment it's placed, and a zero-knowledge proof makes the auctioneer pick the right winner.

pages.title: Confidential loyalty points
pages.description: Customers hold and move loyalty points with hidden amounts on Cardano, wallets recover their balances from chain data, and an auditor can still read every amount.

pages.title: Proof of solvency with hidden balances
pages.description: An exchange proves its locked reserves cover every customer balance while hiding each balance and even the total. Customers and an auditor check their part from on-chain data.

pages.title: Modules
pages.description: Every published ZeroJ artifact with its coordinates, purpose, BOM membership, maturity and main entry-point classes, plus the unpublished support projects.

pages.title: API cheat sheet
pages.description: One page of the ZeroJ calls you use most, grouped by task, each with the class's package, from circuit definition to on-chain verification, BBS, commitments and encryption.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: Every ZeroJ system property, environment variable, native-library requirement, external tool and contributor Gradle flag, and which ones are dev-only.

pages.title: FAQ & troubleshooting
pages.description: Straight answers about ZeroJ's maturity, proof systems, tooling and performance, plus fixes for the errors you are most likely to hit.

pages.title: Migration notes
pages.description: Move from com.bloxbean.cardano to the org.zeroj namespace, to JuLC's org.julclang namespace, and from the pre-cleanup module set to today's focused module surface.

pages.title: Build with AI
pages.description: Give Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot or any chat assistant accurate, versioned ZeroJ context — llms.txt, Markdown twins, a starter pack and an API catalog.

pages.title: AI Starter Pack
pages.description: Everything an AI coding agent needs to write correct ZeroJ code on the first try. Ingest it before generating circuits, proofs or validators.
